questions.questionText: Which safety practice is appropriate when heating a test tube?
questions.explanation: Pointing the test tube away reduces risk from splashes or sudden release.

questions.questionText: A fuse protects a circuit by
questions.explanation: A fuse melts and breaks the circuit when current is excessive.

questions.questionText: Which gas is most abundant in Earth's atmosphere?
questions.explanation: Nitrogen makes up most of Earth's atmosphere.

questions.questionText: Which process in plants transports water mainly through xylem?
questions.explanation: Water moves through xylem as part of the transpiration stream.

questions.questionText: Which instrument measures temperature?
questions.explanation: A thermometer measures temperature.

questions.questionText: A metal that reacts readily with dilute acid often produces
questions.explanation: Reactive metals can displace hydrogen from dilute acids.

questions.questionText: Which component is needed for a complete simple circuit?
questions.explanation: A complete conducting path allows current to flow from the source and back.

questions.questionText: Which environmental problem is strongly associated with excess greenhouse gases?
questions.explanation: Increased greenhouse gases can enhance the greenhouse effect and warming.

questions.questionText: Which reproductive cell is produced by the male human reproductive system?
questions.explanation: Sperm are male gametes.

questions.questionText: A cyclist travels 300 m in 20 s. What is the average speed?
Practical Investigation: Describe how to test a food extract for the presence of (a) protein [2 marks] and (b) fats/lipids [2 marks], stating positive colour/appearance results.
questions.explanation:
(a) Biuret test: add dilute NaOH then a few drops of dilute CuSO₄; a purple/violet colour confirms protein [2 marks].
(b) Emulsion test: shake food extract with ethanol, then pour into water; a cloudy white milky emulsion confirms fat [2 marks].

questions.questionText:
Practical Investigation: A student tests a green leaf for starch after boiling it in water and warming it in ethanol in a water bath.
(a) Explain why the leaf is boiled in water first. [1 mark]
(b) Explain why ethanol is heated in a water bath rather than directly over a Bunsen flame. [2 marks]
(c) State the reagent used and positive result for starch. [2 marks]
questions.explanation:
(a) To kill cells, soften the cuticle, and break cell membranes [1 mark].
(b) Ethanol is highly flammable and would catch fire near an open flame [2 marks].
(c) Iodine solution; turns blue-black in areas containing starch [2 marks].

questions.questionText: Practical Investigation: Describe an experiment using a simple potometer to measure how wind speed affects the rate of transpiration in a leafy shoot. [5 marks]
questions.explanation: Cut leafy shoot under water and seal cleanly into water-filled potometer tubing [1]. Introduce a small air bubble into the capillary tube and measure distance moved along the millimetre scale in 5 minutes in still air [2]. Place an electric fan at a fixed distance to simulate wind and repeat timing over 5 minutes; distance moved increases showing faster transpiration [2].

questions.questionText: Practical Investigation: Explain how to determine the volume and density of an irregular small stone using a displacement (Eureka) can, measuring cylinder, and top-pan balance. [5 marks]
questions.explanation: Weigh dry stone on balance to get mass m (g) [1]. Fill Eureka can with water up to spout until dripping stops, then place dry measuring cylinder under spout [1]. Gently lower tied stone into can until fully submerged and collect overflow water volume V (cm³) [2]. Compute ρ = m / V [1].

questions.questionText: Practical Investigation: Describe how to set up an electrical circuit to verify Ohm's law for a nichrome wire resistor, naming the instruments used and how resistance is found from a graph. [5 marks]
questions.explanation: Connect cell, switch, variable resistor (rheostat), ammeter in series with the nichrome wire, and a voltmeter in parallel across the wire [2]. Adjust rheostat to record 5 pairs of (I, V) readings while keeping temperature steady [2]. Plot V (y-axis) against I (x-axis): straight line through origin verifies Ohm's law, and gradient equals resistance R [1].

questions.questionText:
Practical Investigation: During a titration using a burette, a learner reads initial level = 1.40 cm³ and final level = 23.80 cm³.
(a) Calculate the titre volume delivered. [1 mark]
(b) Why should the conical flask be swirled continuously and placed on a white tile? [2 marks]
questions.explanation:
(a) Titre = 23.80 - 1.40 = 22.40 cm³ [1 mark].
(b) Swirling ensures complete instant mixing; white tile gives a clear background to spot the exact indicator colour change at endpoint [2 marks].

questions.questionText: Practical Investigation: Design an experiment with three test tubes to prove that both water and oxygen are necessary for iron nails to rust. [5 marks]
questions.explanation: Tube A: iron nail in ordinary tap water + air (control — rusts) [1]. Tube B: iron nail in freshly boiled distilled water sealed with an oil layer (no oxygen — no rust) [2]. Tube C: iron nail with anhydrous calcium chloride drying agent + rubber bung (no water — no rust) [2].

questions.questionText:
Practical Investigation: A student investigates germination by placing soaked bean seeds on wet cotton wool at 25°C, in a fridge at 4°C, and on dry cotton wool at 25°C.
(a) State which dishes show germination after 5 days. [1 mark]
(b) What conditions are demonstrated as essential? [2 marks]
(c) State one variable that must be kept constant for a fair test. [1 mark]
questions.explanation:
(a) Only the seeds on wet cotton wool at 25°C germinate [1 mark].
(b) Water (moisture) and suitable warmth/temperature [2 marks].
(c) Seed species/batch, number of seeds per dish, or access to air/oxygen [1 mark].

questions.questionText: Practical Investigation: Outline how to separate pure dry table salt crystals from rock salt (sand + sodium chloride) using simple laboratory apparatus. [5 marks]
questions.explanation: Crush rock salt, stir into warm water in a beaker so NaCl dissolves while sand stays insoluble [2]. Filter through funnel and filter paper to trap sand residue [1]. Evaporate salty filtrate gently in an evaporating basin until crystals start forming, then cool and dry crystals [2].

questions.questionText: Practical Investigation: Describe how to measure the focal length of a convex lens approximately using a distant window and a white screen. [4 marks]
questions.explanation: Hold the convex lens between a distant sunlit object (window/trees) and a white paper screen [1]. Move the screen back and forth until a sharp inverted image appears on the screen [2]. Measure the perpendicular distance from lens centre to screen with a ruler — this equals focal length f [1].

questions.questionText: Practical Investigation: Explain how to investigate the extension of a helical spring under increasing slotted masses up to 500 g and plot results safely. [5 marks]
questions.explanation: Clamp spring vertically beside a metre rule with pointer attached [1]. Record initial pointer reading L₀ with 0 N load [1]. Add 1 N (100 g) weights stepwise up to 5 N, recording new lengths and computing extension e = L - L₀ [2]. Wear eye protection against snapping and plot Load vs Extension to verify proportionality [1].

questions.questionText: Practical Investigation: State the positive chemical tests and expected observations for (a) oxygen gas [2 marks], (b) hydrogen gas [2 marks], and (c) ammonia gas [2 marks].
questions.explanation: (a) Oxygen relights a glowing wooden splint [2 marks]. (b) Hydrogen burns with a squeaky "pop" when a lighted splint is applied [2 marks]. (c) Ammonia turns damp red litmus paper blue (pungent smell) [2 marks].

questions.questionText:
Practical Investigation: A student conducts paper chromatography on black ink using water as solvent.
(a) Why must the baseline be drawn in pencil rather than ink? [2 marks]
(b) Why must the solvent level start below the ink spot? [1 mark]
questions.explanation:
(a) Pencil graphite is insoluble in water so it will not dissolve and smear up the chromatogram; ink would run [2 marks].
(b) So the ink spot separates upward by capillary action rather than dissolving straight down into the solvent beaker [1 mark].

questions.questionText: Practical Investigation: Describe how to use a ray box, plane mirror, protractor, and white paper to verify the law of reflection. [4 marks]
questions.explanation: Draw mirror line and perpendicular normal on paper [1]. Shine a narrow incident ray at angle i (e.g. 30°) to the normal and trace both incident and reflected rays with pencil dots [2]. Measure reflected angle r with protractor and repeat for angles 20°–60°, confirming angle i = angle r [1].

questions.questionText: Practical Investigation: Describe how to observe onion epidermal cells stained with iodine under a light microscope, explaining why iodine stain is added. [4 marks]
questions.explanation: Peel a thin transparent inner onion epidermis layer, place flat in a drop of water on a glass slide, add 1 drop of iodine solution, and lower a coverslip gently at an angle to avoid air bubbles [3 marks]. Iodine stains cell nuclei and cell walls brown/yellow so organelles stand out clearly under the microscope [1 mark].
